ma_corps_wall.blurb: A steep wall on the Hanging Mountain cliff band in Sandisfield, in the far southwest of Massachusetts a few miles from the Connecticut line. About twenty routes, two thirds of them trad and the rest sport, and the grade spread is serious: a handful of 5.9s and 5.10s, a big cluster at 5.11, and several 5.12 and 5.13 lines. This is a place for strong leaders chasing hard, well-regarded testpieces rather than for beginners or a mileage day. Expect a short but steep uphill hike through talus to reach it, and bring a helmet, since loose rock is a feature of the surrounding cliffs.

ma_swingles_quarry.blurb: The largest of the old granite quarries at Quincy Quarries, just south of Boston. It was once a flooded pit and has since been filled in, so the walls are far shorter than they used to be, roughly thirty feet today with the tallest line around sixty. Of the twenty climbs, most are top ropes, with two short trad lines and a single aid route. Grades run from easy 5.2 slabs up to 5.10 cracks and flakes, so there is plenty for newer climbers and a few harder lines for the stronger ones. Features include a dividing wall, a dihedral, several flakes and an arete.

ma_m_wall.blurb: A short top-rope wall in the Granite Railway Quarry, part of the Quincy Quarries climbing area south of Boston. The face runs about ninety feet across and changes character as you move along it: a steep little section with an arete on the left, a low-angle slab that suits kids and first-timers in the middle, and steeper, blockier rock about twenty-five to thirty-five feet tall on the right. Of twenty problems, most are top ropes from 5.3 to 5.10, plus two V2 to V4 boulder problems and a bolt ladder. A third-class descent path runs alongside the left end.

ma_ravenswood_boulder.blurb: A cluster of trailside boulders in Ravenswood Park on Cape Ann, in Gloucester on the North Shore. It holds about twenty bouldering problems spread over several blocks, with a wide range of difficulty: a few easy warm-ups, a good group of V2 and V3 problems, and a surprisingly strong top end that reaches V7 and beyond, including a couple of V8 to V12 testpieces and a famous V10 sit start. A good stop for strong boulderers who want a quiet wooded setting, and a fair number of moderate problems keep it worthwhile for others. Pads and a short walk in on park trails are needed.

ma_harvard_yard.blurb: A bouldering area on wooded conservation land in the town of Harvard, central Massachusetts, reached from the Pin Hill trail network. Scattered rocks and boulders run through the forest, many of them undeveloped and still needing cleaning of moss, lichen and loose pieces, though some blocks are solid. The twenty recorded problems are mostly easy to moderate, with an even spread from V0 through V5 and a single hard line at V7. Expect an adventurous, low-traffic feel rather than a polished circuit, with some line of boulders still waiting to be explored. The trails in are well kept and the walk is gentle apart from one short hill.
